quantity_note: The connectivity v3's encoder constructs between token positions, not a physical DNA/protein interaction claim.
head_invariance_note: There is no head axis (ADR 0008). v3's nine regression heads share one encoder trunk and the rollout is a function of that trunk's attention alone, so one row yields one 5x5 matrix rather than nine. `heads` is recorded only to name the trunk's consumers: no entry of this array belongs to a head, and no per-head rollout figure is derivable from it. The per-head PAM question is answered by ISM (base resolution) and IG (token resolution).
token_resolution_note: Stored at five-token resolution and not unfolded to the 30 base coordinates (ADR 0007): attention is a quantity between tokens, and the last token is 'pam_plus_right_flank' — it binds the PAM (24-26) to the right flank (27-29), so an unfold would re-mix what that ADR separates. The SaCas9 pipeline's 36x36 unfold is not inherited.
layer_operation_note: Per layer, averaged over the encoder's attention heads: the identity is added first (the residual connection's implicit contribution) and the row normalised second. The reverse order gives a different matrix. Layers are combined by left-multiplying each later layer onto the running product.
attention_heads_note: Encoder attention heads, averaged per layer (Abnar & Zuidema, 2020). Unrelated to v3's nine regression heads, which this quantity does not vary over.
attention_implementation_note: `attention_implementation` is the implementation that was actually in force while the probabilities were read, not the one the run asked for. The run switches the model to `eager` wherever it can be switched, because the fused kernels (`sdpa`, flash attention) never materialise the attention probability matrix: under transformers 5.x `output_attentions=True` on an sdpa model returns an empty tuple instead of raising, so a rollout run would have nothing to roll. On a model that cannot report its implementation this field reads `unknown` — older transformers fall back to eager by themselves, so the probabilities are real, but the run has not verified which path produced them.
per_layer_note: The 24 per-layer matrices are ~9 MB and are deliberately not stored: no analysis reads them.
cls_removal_note: `<cls>` participates in the rollout and its row and column are dropped afterwards, so each stored row sums to 1 minus the share that reached `<cls>` (`cls_mass` records that share's distribution). The block is **not** renormalised: rescaling it would state a dependency between sequence tokens that the encoder routed through `<cls>`.
row_index_note: int64, aligned to axis 0 and strictly ascending — the same ordering contract as `ism.npz` and `ig.npz`, so a join is one operation rather than a per-artifact convention.
